channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: Tunisia calls for roadmap to recycle construction waste in roads
item.description: The government says future road projects could use 20 to 30% recycled material, while a trial on the RN3 tests durability.

item.title: Sierra Leone regulator reports NLE 7.4 million in 2024 revenue
item.description: The electricity and water commission said revenue from levies and licenses rose from NLE 2.3 million in 2023.

item.title: Sierra Leone's vice presidency has never produced an elected president
item.description: A February analysis by public policy analyst Foday M. Daboh says the office has often left its holders without an independent political base or a path to succession.

item.title: Sierra Leone charcoal trade sustains livelihoods as tree loss threatens food security
item.description: A 65-year-old burner says his family depends on the trade, while the Environmental Protection Agency warns that producers are cutting fruit trees.

item.title: Nigeria targets 1.4 million tonnes of milk a year within five years
item.description: The livestock minister also set out a potential $3.2 billion beef export market, saying the figure represents an opportunity, not current earnings.

item.title: Nigeria opposition candidate pledges N200 petrol and free healthcare in 2027
item.description: Adewole Adebayo, candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), says his government would cut the price without subsidy and provide free medical consultations and medication.

item.title: Ivorian minister urges study of ratings body for social-security funds
item.description: Adama Kamara proposed assessing whether CIPRES could rate member funds, helping them build financial credibility and secure financing.

item.title: South Sudan sets December 12 launch for Boma-Badingilo heritage site
item.description: The landscape was inscribed in July as the country’s first UNESCO World Heritage Site, but is also listed as being in danger.

item.title: Somalia leaves transport minister’s armed confrontation unanswered
item.description: A video showed State Minister Abdikarim Abdow Hayder carrying an AK-47 to the ministry gates amid a dispute over vehicle number-plate kickbacks.

item.title: IMF approves $425 million programme for Guinea, leaves subsidy cuts to government
item.description: The 2026-2029 deal calls for a strategy to reduce subsidies, while Guinea decides when to act and strengthens support for vulnerable households.

item.title: Nurse takes newborn home for oxygen after Malawi clinic loses power
item.description: The baby was stabilised at the nurse’s home and referred to Mitundu Community Hospital, while the clinic’s outage has lasted about two and a half months.

item.title: Tinubu points to waivers for 75 drug makers as he builds health economy
item.description: Between January 2025 and June 2026, more than ₦24 billion in tax and tariff relief was approved for the manufacturers.

item.title: Namibia delays national airline launch to June 2027
item.description: The Ministry of Works and Transport says aircraft delivery delays have moved the planned start of commercial flights from December 2026.

item.title: South Sudan youth groups press for 20% representation in government
item.description: An assessment found little improvement from last year, while the country has no legislature in place for a new parliamentary count.

item.title: Cape Verde security essay calls for lasting prevention and police coordination
item.description: Domingos Barbosa da Silva says short-lived community policing and weak information-sharing leave the causes of crime unaddressed.

item.title: Casamance women’s peace platform urges inquiry into Oulampane mayor attack
item.description: The group called for calm and said authorities must establish responsibility after the mayor was seriously burned while asleep on 26 November.

item.title: Equatorial Guinea prioritises household power as Malabo turbine repair drags on
item.description: The vice-president ordered the state electricity company, Sociedad de Electricidad de Guinea Ecuatorial (SEGESA), to favour homes over street lighting while a damaged turbine is.

item.title: Equatorial Guinea hands regional presidency to Chad
item.description: Chad will lead the Central African Economic Community’s work, with security, economic cooperation and regional institutions on its agenda.

item.title: Korhogo prosecutor warns police over detainees’ rights
item.description: Souleymane Koné said officers must respect legal custody limits and detainees’ rights to a lawyer, a doctor and contact with a relative.

item.title: Mali grants Roscan Gold Mali a 12-year gold mining permit
item.description: The permit covers Kandiolé-Nord in Kayes region, where exploration found a deposit that can be mined economically on a large scale.

item.title: Sierra Leone passes 2027 finance bill with tax changes
item.description: The amended bill sets out revenue measures including a Le10 annual poll tax and a 20% surcharge on qualifying imported goods.

item.title: Tshopo officials meet Bafwasende youth on restarting Ebola response
item.description: Provincial ministers for the interior and health joined response workers for talks with young people in the Tshopo town.

item.title: Study says Lagos sinks 5mm a year, raising flood risk
item.description: The study links the city's annual sinking rate with increased exposure to flooding, but the report provides no further details.

item.title: Kiambu court order halts 72 million litres of daily water supply
item.description: The county government obtained interim orders barring Kenya's national water agency from supplying six providers that serve homes and businesses.

item.title: Togo opens 17-day Lomé trade fair with India as guest of honour
item.description: The event brings exhibitors, investors and business operators from Togo and other countries to CETEF TOGO, a conference and exhibition centre in Lomé, through 13 December.

item.title: United ATS opens Tunis aviation training centre for regional clients
item.description: The company says local training, priced in Tunisian dinars, can replace services that aviation customers currently buy abroad.

item.title: Togo brings 176 citizens home from Mali after departures from Guinea
item.description: The government received the returnees at three sites and is still identifying Togolese in Burkina Faso who want to come home.

item.title: Benin seeks CFA181,9 billion for farm investment and higher output
item.description: The proposed 2027 budget targets 724 281 tonnes of cotton, alongside higher cereal and soybean harvests.

item.title: Mauritius approves 124-point blue economy strategy for 2026-2035
item.description: The Cabinet approved a decade-long plan covering ocean-linked industries, with a new council to coordinate its implementation across government.

item.title: Mali eye hospital treats more than 300 displaced people for cataracts
item.description: The Bamako hospital also received specialist equipment worth more than CFA250 million, funded by Spain through its development agency and a foundation partner.

item.title: Togo opposition calls for urgent search for missing priest
item.description: Four opposition groups, including the Manifeste Génération Togo, urged authorities to find Father Éric Ébélaki, a vicar in Kara, and return him safely.

item.title: Mauritius ministers note NEF consultations with 130 participants
item.description: The third regional session brought beneficiaries and community representatives together in Quartier-Militaire on 26 November.

item.title: GMet forecasts 39°C heat in Bolgatanga and Nalerigu
item.description: The weather service also expects late-afternoon rain or thunderstorms in parts of the coast and forest belt.

item.title: Algerians vote for local councils as 162,864 candidates compete
item.description: The ballot selects members of municipal and provincial assemblies across 1,541 communes and 69 wilayas for five-year terms.

item.title: Zimbabwe needs US$52.78 million to clear remaining landmines by 2030
item.description: Deputy Defence Minister Levy Mayihlome says more than 97% of contaminated land has been cleared, with about 22,000 households set to benefit.

item.title: Headspring gets approval for Stampriet uranium research boreholes
item.description: The company says it will use no chemical reagents in the research phase and plans to submit a revised pilot-testing application.

item.title: Mauritius unions challenge 4.7% inflation rate in 2027 wage talks
item.description: Workers’ representatives say the 2026 figure understates living costs as tripartite consultations on salary compensation get under way.

item.title: Ravatomanga family seeks answers over search of its tomb
item.description: Lawyers say people claiming a prosecutor’s mandate searched the family tomb in Moratsiazo and reported finding nothing.

item.title: Madagascar's ousted Assembly president asks court to annul his removal
item.description: Siteny Randrianasoloniaiko's petition also challenges the removal of three other bureau members, arguing the required serious grounds were not shown.

item.title: Beugré Mambé urges cashew sector to exceed 57% local processing
item.description: The prime minister made the appeal at the opening of the cashew-processing equipment and technology fair in Treichville on 26 November.

item.title: Museveni directs Uganda to identify island site for proposed resort
item.description: The UK-based investor says it is considering tourism projects, while three international hotel groups are in talks to build hotels in Uganda.

item.title: Central African Republic collects far less from mining and forests than it could
item.description: World Bank-commissioned experts say enforcing the new mining code could double or triple state revenue from the two sectors.

item.title: Malawian actress Yvonne Scott wins role in Nigerian film
item.description: The creative team behind Ikenga: The Last Festival selected Scott after her performances in Malawi’s entertainment industry.

item.title: Kenya's savings co-operatives face money-laundering gaps as grey-list exit effort conti...
item.description: Financial sector experts say weak monitoring, member checks and reporting systems leave the societies exposed to abuse and short of compliance capacity.

item.title: Uganda charges six over alleged USh13 billion road compensation fraud
item.description: Prosecutors say inflated claims for structures on the planned Kasanje-Mpigi Expressway could have cost the government more than USh13 billion.

item.title: Madagascar plans more water for Antananarivo's outskirts
item.description: Three station upgrades are planned to add 10 800 m³ of drinking water a day to Jirama's network and serve districts around the capital.

item.title: Madagascar Oil supplies fuel for RN1 Bis rehabilitation
item.description: The company provided 7 000 litres for heavy machinery used by military engineers working to improve access before the rains.

item.title: Madagascar's finance minister urges stronger university research support
item.description: At the University of Antananarivo's 65th anniversary ceremony, he cited renewable energy and called for research to shape development projects.

item.title: Malawi U-17 players complain about camp food and living conditions
item.description: Members of the boys' and girls' squads said the diet and conditions in their Lilongwe camp at times made them feel dehumanised.

item.title: Malawi Revenue Authority suspends officer over sexual misconduct complaint
item.description: The authority says Jonathan Sulumba will remain suspended while it investigates an Irish visitor's allegation about an incident at its Lilongwe office.

item.title: Eswatini engineer builds Chicago career in public infrastructure
item.description: Vuyiswa Mngometulu, a 2023 Northwestern graduate, works on water networks, sewers, roads and stormwater systems for a Chicago firm.

item.title: Blantyre-area water customers pay extra during supply cuts
item.description: Chatha resident Elizabeth Tembo says interruptions leave her buying bottled water and paying workers to fetch borehole water, on top of her monthly bills.

item.title: Cameroon plans CFA50 billion more in annual beverage taxes
item.description: The 2027 finance bill would raise excise duties and add a CFA5 stamp duty to each bottled drink.

item.title: Simão Mendes hospital workers press for 11 months of overdue allowances
item.description: The hospital administrator says the government committed to pay three months, while staff also seek eight months of pay for contract workers.

item.title: Mauritania raises pensions and public-sector pay from January
item.description: The changes include a monthly 10 000 old-ouguiya supplement for all civilian and military retirees, with a minimum pension of 50 000.

item.title: Senegal’s anti-corruption body targets 50% score with Forum Civil
item.description: The partners are beginning a self-assessment after Senegal remained in the red zone of Transparency International’s corruption index since 1998.

item.title: Burkina Faso restarts Perkoa mine after four years idle
item.description: The state mining company has resumed operations at the polymetallic site, closed since April 2022 after underground flooding killed eight workers.

item.title: Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger approve digital cooperation framework
item.description: The agreement covers connected networks, postal services and cybersecurity, with diplomatic review and leaders’ approval still ahead.

item.title: Regional body adopts Djibouti’s anti-money-laundering report
item.description: The evaluation recognised reforms and stronger coordination, while examining how the country’s rules work in practice.

item.title: Chad’s Déby takes CEEAC chair, pledges focus on implementation
item.description: The Central African bloc’s new leader set out priorities including peace, security, economic integration and infrastructure development.

item.title: Civil society groups reject Ghana's five-year presidential term proposal
item.description: More than 100 groups also want citizens to elect local leaders without presidential shortlisting in the proposed metropolitan, municipal and district chief executive system.

item.title: Kuapa Kokoo warns illegal mining and erratic weather are cutting cocoa output
item.description: Managing Director Emmanuel Kwabena Arthur says pods are scarce at the harvest peak, while polluted rivers leave farmers without clean water.

item.title: Guinea plans new fuel depot and reforms power utility
item.description: Economy Minister Mariama Ciré Sylla says studies for the depot are complete as the government works to improve the utility’s governance.

item.title: Senegal deploys more than 3 500 personnel for eastern security exercise
item.description: Boundou 2026 runs in Tambacounda and Kédougou from 28 November to 6 December, with free medical consultations also planned in some localities.

item.title: Adenka opens Djibouti office to serve businesses and investors
item.description: The Abidjan-based audit network says its Djibouti team will offer accounting, tax and risk advice alongside audits and project assurance.

item.title: Niger transport director warns Tahoua carriers of firm rule enforcement
item.description: At a meeting on Friday, Oumarou Ibrahim urged freight and fuel operators to curb overloading and keep vehicles, papers and drivers compliant.

item.title: Ru’ya warns of up to 100 millimeters of rain in northwest Libya
item.description: The foundation says the heaviest downpours are expected around Tripoli and along the coast, with flash floods and road disruption possible.

item.title: Guinea’s U15 schoolgirls take second place and 75 000 dollars US
item.description: The team earned 5 points in Monrovia, won the tournament’s fair-play award and missed the only qualifying place for the continental finals.

item.title: Chad pilgrimage regulator chief denies alleged UAE account transfers
item.description: A judicial document cites transfers of 20 million and 16.5 million dirhams from the regulator’s accounts to a personal account at First Abu Dhabi Bank.

item.title: South Sudan urges partners to back national control of peace process
item.description: Foreign Affairs Minister Cecilia Adut Manyok said the African Union, the Intergovernmental Authority on Development and the UN task force should help end the transition, not.

item.title: Burkina Faso’s social security fund honours nine firms for workplace safety
item.description: The first national occupational health and safety prize recognised companies in mining, construction, industry and services at Kaya’s three-day event.

item.title: Burkina Faso mini-dairies seek role in public milk initiatives
item.description: The network collected 1 838 849 litres of local milk and reported more than CFA1.3 billion in revenue in 2025.

item.title: Mauritania intercepts 94 young Guineans bound for the Canary Islands
item.description: Mauritanian coast guards stopped the boat off Nouadhibou on 19 November, and the group is now being housed in Rosso while it waits for travel documents.

item.title: Algeria plans tighter well controls as El Menia groundwater falls
item.description: The agriculture minister says farm expansion must match local water supplies and plans wider use of efficient irrigation and treated wastewater.

item.title: Guinea suspends Infosbruts and director for three months
item.description: The media regulator said the site published electoral propaganda for a Lélouma Senate candidate before the Supreme Court issued its final candidate list.

item.title: EU, US and partners urge Sudan's warring sides to open aid routes
item.description: A joint warning says 19.5 million people face acute food insecurity and calls for support for Sudan's winter planting season.

item.title: Ramaphosa backs urgent efforts to end Sudan war
item.description: The South African president voiced concern over worsening humanitarian conditions after Abdullah Hamdok’s delegation presented a Sudanese-led political plan.

item.title: Darar and Demil win Air Djibouti 10 km races
item.description: Aden Waberi Darar finished the men's race in 27 min 36 sec, while Kaira Mohamed Demil won the women's event in 33 min 40 sec.

item.title: Cuba seeks to restart health fairs in remote Equatorial Guinea
item.description: The Cuban ambassador says the events would bring specialist care and early disease detection to isolated communities.

item.title: Rwenzori farmers earn carbon income by planting trees
item.description: A Kasese farmer has received USh880,000 since 2021, while agroforestry is also supporting crops and livestock on his land.

item.title: Nalolo steps up El Niño measures to protect farmers and livestock
item.description: Officials in the district are preparing communities and farmers for the expected weather shock, with food security as the goal.

item.title: Bank of Zambia holds policy rate at 10.75%
item.description: Annual inflation edged up to 6.4% in November, while actual and projected inflation remain within the bank’s 6 to 8% target band.

item.title: Zambia's youth group praises Imisepela platform for jobs and funding
item.description: The Back to School Youth Initiative Group says the government platform has registered more than 300,000 young people and disbursed over K18.3 million to youth-led businesses.

item.title: Zambia urges weather agencies to build systems that protect livelihoods
item.description: Permanent Secretary Douty Chibamba called on participants at a Lusaka workshop to strengthen cross-border weather intelligence.

item.title: L’Archer chief calls for legal, finance and business reforms in Congo
item.description: Gilles Tchamba says clear state rules, bolder entrepreneurs and finance that channels savings to businesses are needed for a healthier business climate.

item.title: Congo minister urges mindset reform to attract private investors
item.description: Denis Christel Sassou Nguesso says administrative conduct is driving investors to seek more favourable conditions in other countries.

item.title: Chad's mediator denies Kebzabo warned of civil war
item.description: The institution rejected an online outlet's account of his remarks and urged media and social-media users to report them accurately.

item.title: Chad aid reaches 2.5 million people as funding covers 46.3% of needs
item.description: The response had reached 75% of its initial target by 30 September, but nearly one million people in need remained without assistance.

item.title: Niger opens 100-place centre for children facing family difficulties
item.description: The Niamey facility, built with the NGO International Humanitarian Relief Foundation (IHH), includes classrooms, dormitories and a medical and social services building.

item.title: Benin's social security fund moves employer filings and payments online
item.description: From 1 December, employers must use the national public-services portal for registration certificates and social-contribution payments.

item.title: FAO and WFP warn of worsening food insecurity risk in Angola
item.description: The agencies cite drought, expected cereal-production declines and the risk of a late start to the next rainy season.

item.title: Timimoun hosts Polish delegation for talks on farm investment
item.description: The visitors examined prospects for investment in strategic crops and partnerships with Algerian operators at the Tinerkouk El-Kebir farm area.

item.title: Sierra Leone Parliament receives five public-service audit reports
item.description: The reports, dated August 2026, examine building permits, maternal health, emergency care, electricity generation, education and waste management.

item.title: Burundi's election commission rejects Rwasa's presidential bid
item.description: The commission says he failed to prove he had been outside party politics for at least a year, while his representative plans an appeal.

item.title: Tshisekedi to press central African summit on UN resolution 2773
item.description: The DR Congo president arrived in Malabo on Friday 27 November for the 27th summit of the Economic Community of Central African States (ECCAS), the regional bloc.

item.title: Morocco tightens surveillance for 124,971 teacher exam candidates
item.description: The Education Ministry ordered online monitoring and automated cheating detection, with no more than 20 candidates in each room.

item.title: Mashaba returns as Johannesburg mayor, beating the DA's Helen Zille
item.description: The ActionSA leader was elected at a council sitting, after coalition talks involving the ANC, ActionSA and the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) party.

item.title: Solar industry body urges Tunisia to revisit rejected tax cuts
item.description: The photovoltaic chamber wants lawmakers to reconsider lower import duties on solar panels and exemptions for storage batteries in the 2027 finance bill.

item.title: Chad's administration school receives equipment from China
item.description: The Chinese embassy donated computer and office tools to the national school, alongside a discussion on lessons from China's development.

item.title: Congo and Uganda agree to settle security row through diplomacy
item.description: Kinshasa had summoned Uganda's mission chief after posts by Uganda's army chief about eastern Congo, and Uganda has announced it will withdraw troops from Lubero.
